title: Impacts of Hydroelectric Dams on Amazonian Fisheries: Assessing Functional Attributes in the Madeira River
content:
ABSTRACT

The Madeira River is one of the main tributaries of the Amazon Basin, supporting over 1300 known fish species. Fisheries in this region play a critical role for riverine populations, serving as a primary source of income and sustenance. In 2011, the construction of the Jirau and Santo Antônio hydroelectric dams (HEDs) was completed along the Madeira River. This study offers insights to improve environmental management of large-scale hydroelectric projects in the Amazon. To assess the impacts of the dams on fish species and environmental characteristics, we analyzed migration patterns and habitat preferences of fish landed at the ports of Humaitá (downstream) and Guajará-Mirim (upstream) from 2000 to 2019, comparing pre- and post-construction periods. Our findings reveal a significant decline in regional fish migration, with reductions of 85.5% upstream and 51.6% downstream, highlighting migratory species as the most affected. Habitat-specific impacts were also observed, with benthopelagic species declining by 70.5% upstream and 51.3% downstream, and pelagic species experiencing reductions of 82.2% upstream and 41.8% downstream. The hydroelectric project triggered an abrupt decrease in fishery production, altering the structure of fish communities. The results also indicate greater fishing pressure on local fish stocks, which underscores the urgency of revisiting current environmental management practices to mitigate the environmental and social impacts of such projects.
